requirement: Provide a pytest assertion helper that checks an expected JSON-like subset against an actual payload, allowing extra dict keys but requiring equal list lengths and exact scalar types, and raising AssertionError that names the path of the first mismatch while hiding its own frames.
skeleton: assert_subset with __tracebackhide__, a dict branch checking type, key presence and recursing with dotted paths, a list branch checking length and recursing with indexed paths, and a scalar branch comparing type and value.
caption: A custom pytest assertion helper for JSON-like payloads that raises AssertionError naming the path of the first mismatch, with no third-party library beyond pytest. assert_subset(actual, expected, path="$") sets __tracebackhide__ so pytest hides the helper's own frames and points at the calling test. When expected is a dict, actual must also be a dict or it raises AssertionError saying expected an object, got the actual type name; every expected key must be present, even when its value is None, or it raises missing key with the repr of the key, and each value is checked recursively under the path extended with a dot and the key, while extra keys in actual are allowed. When expected is a list, actual must be a list of the same length or it raises expected N items, got the actual length, and items are compared pairwise under the path extended with the bracketed index. Any other expected value must have exactly the same type and compare equal, so True never matches 1, otherwise it raises the repr of actual, !=, and the repr of expected. The fixture asserts that subsets with extra keys and a None value pass, that a wrong second role reports $.user.roles[1], that a missing email key is named, that shorter and longer role lists report their lengths, that True against 1 fails, that a dict expected against an int fails, and that __tracebackhide__ is among the helper's local variables.

plan.intent: Get readable failures when asserting on API payloads
constraints: Mismatches raise AssertionError naming the dotted and indexed path
Extra dict keys are allowed but missing keys fail even when the expected value is None
Lists must have the same length
Scalars must match in type and value
The helper hides its frames with __tracebackhide__

rationale.teaches: Writing recursive assertion helpers with path-bearing AssertionError messages and __tracebackhide__ for pytest.
rationale.why: A helper that loses the path, truncates lists or treats True as 1 passes wrong payloads or fails with messages nobody can act on.

ops.docstring: A pytest assertion helper that reports the JSON path of the first mismatch.

candidates.why_wrong: List items reuse the parent path, so the failing index never appears in the message.
Lengths are not compared and zip stops at the shorter list, so extra or missing items pass.
Without the type check True equals 1, so a boolean passes where an integer was expected.
get returning None is taken as missing, so a key whose value is None is reported absent.
Joining the checks with and only fails when both type and value differ, so wrong strings pass.
